1  ORDER
This petition has been filed to quash the FIR registered in Cr.No.31 of 2023 on the file of the first respondent.
2. The case of the prosecution is that the defacto complainant is running a business of Yarn Trading at Tiruppur.
She is having business relation with the petitioners.

Thereby, the defacto complainant has delivered cotton yarn, viscose yarn, viscose fabric, cotton fabric and cotton garments to the following four concerns run by these petitioners 1) TD TEX FAB (Rs.2,16,18,016/-) , 2) Pwalls Overseas Ltd., (Rs.1,75,77,234/-), 3) Rajasthan Impex (Rs.3,10,86,731/-) and 4) JSR Corporation (Rs.3,02,17,903/-) to the tune of Rs.Rs.10,04,99,884/-,
out of which, the petitioners have made payments to the tune of Rs.4,64,40,552/- and there is an outstanding payment of Rs.5,40,59,332/-
The defacto complainant demanded the outstanding payment, but the petitioners have failed to clear the payment of above mentioned delivery.
All these three people have colluded and planned this scam in a very professional manner.

The main intention of these people is to only loot people by buying goods at market rate and sell it at lesser rate as https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:50 pm ) compared to the market, so that they can immediately liquidate the goods and enjoy the amount by not paying to their suppliers.
Thereby, the petitioners have deceived and cheated the second respondent/defacto complainant.
Hence, the second respondent lodged the complaint before the first respondent police.

Based on the said complaint dated 12.12.2023, the first respondent has registered an FIR as against the petitioners in Cr.No.31 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 120B, 406 and 420 of IPC.
3.
The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are arrayed as A1 to A3 in Cr.No.31 of 2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 406 and 420 of IPC.
For the very same allegation, the second respondent has lodged a complaint before the Inspector of Police, Narpoli Police Station, Bhiwandi, Thane City, Maharashtra on 20.06.2023.

Since, no action has been taken by the police as against the accused persons, the second respondent has filed a private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No.10, Bhiwandi, Maharashtra and sought for direction under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C.

Infact so many FIRs' have been registered in various States in India as against the petitioners and it is sent for investigation.

8. The learned counsel for the second respondent further submits that the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Surat has also issued Production warrant as against the petitioners in Cr.No.31 of 2023 for the offences under Sections 120B, 406 and 420 of IPC.

Therefore, after having been assured to pay the costs of goods, after receipt of the same, the petitioners have failed to pay a huge amount,
nearly Rs.5,40,59,332/- https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Therefore, offence under Section 420 of IPC is clearly made out as against the petitioner.

Further,
it is only an FIR and it cannot be quashed .

9. The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) appearing for the respondent police reiterated the prosecution case, submits that the petitioners have deceived and cheated the second respondent/defacto complainant to the tune of Rs.5,40,59,332/- .
He also confirms that initially, the second respondent lodged a complaint before the Inspector of Police, Bhiwandi, Maharashtra.
Thereafter, the second respondent has withdrawn the complaint from the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No.10, Bhiwandi, Maharashtra.

Hence, he prays for dismissal.

10. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, the learned counsel (Crl.Side)
appearing for the first respondent police and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
09/05/2025 09:14:50 pm ) the learned counsel appearing for the second respondent/defacto complainant and perused the materials available on record.
11.
A perusal of the FIR revealed that on the order placed by the petitioners, the second respondent had supplied yarn on several occasions.
The total outstanding is more than Rs.10,00,00,000, out of which, the petitioners have paid Rs.4,64,40.552/-.

According to the second respondent, the Pankaj Agarwal vs The State Represented By on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122900130/
3 outstanding payment to be received is Rs.5,40,59,322/- Therefore, it is purely a commercial transaction between the petitioners and the second respondent.

Hence, no offence is made out under Section 420 of IPC.
12.
The defacto complainant has alleged in the complaint that the petitioners have committed offences under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
It would thus be necessary to examine the ingredients of the above offences and whether the allegations made in the complaint, read on their face, attract those offences under the India Penal Code.

Section 405 of Indian Penal Code reads thus:-
405. Criminal breach of trust  Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:50 pm ) property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits "criminal breach of trust".

A careful reading of Section 405 of IPC shows that the ingredients of a criminal breach of trust are as follows:-
(i) A person should have been entrusted with property, or entrusted with dominion over property;
(ii) That person should dishonestly misappropriate or convert to their own use that property, or dishonestly use or dispose of that property or willfully suffer any other person to do so; and (iii) That such misappropriation, conversion, use or disposal should be in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or o f a n y l e g a l c o n t r a c t w h i c h t h e p e r s o n h a s m a d e , t o u c h i n g t h e https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:50 pm )
discharge of such trust.
Entrustment is an essential ingredient of the offence.

A person who dishonestly misappropriates property entrusted to them contrary to the terms of an obligation imposed is liable for a criminal breach of trust and is punishable under Section 406 of the Penal Code.

13. It is relevant to extract the provisions under Section 420 of the Penal Code as follows :-
420. Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property  Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a Pankaj Agarwal vs The State Represented By on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122900130/
4
valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

14. The ingredients to constitute an offence under Section 420 of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:50 pm ) IPC are as follows :-
(i) A person must commit the offence of cheating under Section 415 and (ii) The person cheated must be dishonestly induced to (a) deliver property to any person or (b) make, alter or destroy valuable security or anything signed or sealed and capable of being converted into valuable security.
Cheating is an essential ingredient for an act to constitute an offence under Section 420.
15.
In view of the above, the offence under Section 420 of IPC is not at all made out against the petitioners.

As rightly pointed out by the petitioners that originally, the second respondent has lodged a complaint before the Inspector of Police, Narpoli Police Station, Bhiwandi, Thane City,
Maharashtra and the same was enquired and closed as civil in nature.

Thereafter, the second respondent has filed a private complaint before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No.10, Bhiwandi, Maharashtra and sought for a direction to forward the complaint under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C to the concerned jurisdictional Police.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No.10, Bhiwandi, Maharashtra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
However, the learned Judicial Magistrate has rejected the said https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 09/05/2025 09:14:50 pm )
requests and had taken the complaint on file to take cognizance directly.
However, before taking cognizance by the learned Magistrate, the second respondent had withdrawn the complaint.
On the said requests, the learned Magistrate by an order dated 16.07.2024 discharged the accused persons 1 to 4 for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 120B r/w 34 of IPC.

The Learned Magistrate further observed that since the complainant does not want to proceed with the complaint, the powers under Section 245 of Cr.P.C have to be invoked and that no case against the accused has been made out which, if rebutted would warrant his conviction.
Accordingly, the accused were discharged.

16. However, suppressing the above said facts, the second respondent lodged a complaint before the first respondent and managed to register FIR which is impugned in this petition for the offences under Sections 120B, 406 and 420 of IPC.
17.
It is a business transaction and after placing order, the petitioners have received goods after making payment.
Therefore, no offence is made out as against the petitioners and the second respondent ought to have approached the City Civil Court for appropriate relief.

In view of the above, the entire FIR is nothing but clear abuse https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (

Therefore, the FIR registered in Cr.No.31 of 2023 cannot be sustained as against the accused in Cr.No.31 of 2023 on the file of the first respondent and it is liable to be quashed.
Accordingly, it is hereby quashed.
20. In the result, this Criminal Original petition is allowed.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
